purpose: Implements a review analytics dashboard with accuracy metrics tracking — MetricsService, review_metrics table, /metrics Probot command, and GitHub Action summary output. All 8 iteration-1 issues were fixed correctly.
riskRationale: Additive analytics layer on existing LearningStore infrastructure. No existing functionality modified or removed. Remaining issues are minor or limited to the JSON fallback backend and auto-fixable.

text: Clean, well-architected implementation with proper separation of concerns (MetricsService decoupled from LearningStore), consistent patterns across all three backends (SQLite, SqlAdapter, JSON), and comprehensive test coverage. All 8 previously-reported issues were correctly resolved in iteration 1. Two new issues found: JSON backend P50 percentile uses nearest-rank while SQL backends interpolate (important), and JSON backend treats null tokens_used as 0 instead of excluding like SQL AVG() does (important). Three minor issues also noted.

reasoning: All critical and important issues affect only the JSON fallback path — SQL backends (primary storage) are correct. Remaining JSON issues are self-contained, straightforward to fix, and don't block merge of the core functionality. Both SQL backends and the action/app integrations are production-ready.

message: MetricsService cleanly consumes LearningStore without backend coupling — getReport concurrently queries 5 data sources via Promise.all for efficient report assembly.
All 6 analytics delegate methods use try/catch with sensible default return values, consistent with the project's graceful degradation pattern.
P50 percentile in both SqlAdapter and SqliteAdapter correctly averages the two middle elements for even-length arrays, matching the median computation in getLatencyStats.
Full in-memory implementations for all 6 analytics methods in JSON backend, matching SQL backends feature-for-feature — important for users without native database support.
sinceDays correctly computed from period type (1 for daily, 7 for weekly) — fixes the iteration-1 hardcoded-90 bug, making /metrics daily and /metrics weekly produce meaningfully different windows.

Comprehensive test coverage: empty store, seeded data, date filtering, formatReport markdown, null scores, trends, computeAggregation, pre-computed fallback, and JSON database fallback — all with specific value assertions.

P50 percentile in getPerPRStats uses nearest-rank (Math.floor(counts.length * 0.5)) instead of averaging the two middle elements for even-length arrays. Both SQL backends (SqlAdapter db.ts:750-752, SqliteAdapter db.ts:1863-1865) correctly interpolate, but the JSON backend was missed. For counts [10, 20, 30, 40]: JSON returns P50=30, SQL returns P50=25 — a real cross-backend inconsistency.
suggestion: Replace nearest-rank with the same interpolation pattern used in the SQL backends and in getLatencyStats: average the two middle elements for even-length arrays.

message: JSON aggregateMetrics treats null tokens_used as 0 (via ?? 0 coercion) when computing avg_tokens_per_review, while SQL's AVG(tokens_used) ignores NULL values entirely. For 2 quality rows with tokens_used=[100, null]: JSON computes avg=50, SQL computes avg=100. The same null-vs-zero discrepancy affects total_tokens_used (line 1017). The duration_ms field at line 964 correctly filters nulls with .filter((d): d is number => d != null), so the token aggregation should follow the same pattern.
suggestion: Filter out null tokens_used before computing both totalTokens and the row count denominator, matching the duration_ms approach at line 964.

message: truePositiveRate defaults to 1 (100%) when totalFeedback is 0. With no feedback data, claiming 100% true positive rate is semantically misleading. The test at metrics.test.ts:44 explicitly checks this value, so this is a design choice, but a more accurate default would be 0 or null.
suggestion: Change the default tpRate to 0 when there is no feedback, or make it nullable in the interface with 'N/A' rendering in formatReport — matching the pattern used for accuracyScore/actionabilityScore (metrics.ts:130-137).

message: Unknown-severity findings are counted in totalSeverity (line 98-102 includes severityDist.unknown) so the section conditionally renders, but the output string on line 105 omits the unknown count. If findings exist with no severity set, the section appears but the count is incomplete.
suggestion: Add the unknown count to the severity output string alongside critical, important, and minor.

message: Manual ID construction using template literal (f_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}) instead of calling generateId() which produces identical output. Same pattern at db.ts:2017 and json-db.ts:1034. generateId() is already imported and used throughout the codebase — this duplication makes refactoring harder.
suggestion: Replace manual ID construction with generateId() in all three locations.
